## CVD shared preparation plus a separate mortality pathway

The BNR now has two analytical starting routes.

The **CVD events pathway** begins with the CVD REDCap release. Its first three steps form the common private preparation layer used by CVD event metrics, tabulations and routine briefings.

The **CVD mortality pathway** begins with the mortality death-certificate REDCap source. It has its own six-step route because mortality extraction, classification, reporting structure and disclosure controls are different.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["CVD REDCap release"] --> B["CVD events Step 1<br/>Private REDCap extract"]
    B --> C["CVD events Step 2<br/>Confidential cumulative dataset"]
    C --> D["CVD events Step 3<br/>Deidentified analytical inputs"]

    D --> E["CVD event metrics<br/>Steps 4-6"]
    D --> F["Tabulations<br/>Steps 1-3"]
    D --> G["Routine briefings<br/>Steps 1-3"]

    M["Mortality REDCap death-certificate source"] --> N["CVD mortality workflow<br/>Steps 1-6"]

    E --> H["Approved public outputs"]
    F --> H
    G --> H
    N --> H

    H --> I["Quarto publishing layer"]
    I --> J["BNR Info-Hub"]
```

## How the routes differ

| Workflow | Private analytical input | What the workflow then owns |
|---|---|---|
| **CVD event metrics** | Purpose-specific Step 3 metric input, currently `count` for the burden family | Metric calculation, disclosure control, review, approval and metric publication. |
| **CVD mortality** | Mortality Step 1 death-certificate extract, followed by the approved Step 2 classifier | Mortality classification, burden metrics, mortality-specific disclosure control, review, approval and publication. |
| **Tabulations** | CVD Step 3 `all_variables` | Seven routine table calculations, table-specific suppression, review, approval and table publication. |
| **Routine briefings** | CVD Step 3 `count`, `case_fatality` or `length_of_stay`, depending on the briefing | Analyst-owned calculations and figures, human disclosure review, approval and briefing-package publication. |

The CVD Step 3 products remain private. Tabulations and CVD briefings **do not rebuild the confidential cumulative dataset** and should not repeat the CVD Steps 1-3 preparation logic.

Mortality does not branch from CVD Step 3. Its own source, classification and six-step publication contract are documented in [CVD mortality workflow](mortality/overview.qmd).

## Ad-hoc briefings

The ad-hoc briefing pathway is deliberately more flexible.

An ad-hoc analysis is created in an analyst-owned DO file rather than through the routine Briefing Step 1 dispatcher. The analyst must declare the source and create the standard private staging package. The package then joins the common briefing controls at **Briefing Step 2: Review and approve** and **Briefing Step 3: Publish**, using the exact ad-hoc package ID.

For registry analyses, use an appropriate approved deidentified analytical source wherever the analysis permits. Any different source must be explicitly recorded in the briefing release metadata.

The operational CVD mortality dashboard workflow is separate from the briefing dispatcher. A future mortality-rate briefing remains a separate analytical product unless and until it is migrated into that controlled briefing route.

## Compute and publish remain separate

Stata creates and controls the analytical products. Quarto consumes approved public products.

The one documented publication-layer convenience calculation is the mortality dashboard year-to-date count. Its narrow rules are described in [Maintain the CVD mortality dashboard](../website/cvd-mortality-dashboard.qmd); it does not establish a general analytical pathway in Quarto.

Updating narrative pages, dashboards, listings or other website content is covered under **Operate the Info-Hub**, not inside the analytical workflow steps.
